# dsh-chapters

**Long memory for local AI: a DeepSeek Harness
plugin that archives agent conversations as verbatim

chapters, continues sessions from a Table of
Contents at zero inference-token cost, and turns that a

rchive into a shared, searchable knowledge
pool.** Published on npm as `@fractalsynapse/dsh-chapters

`;
source at fractalsynapse/dsh-chapters.
> **All documentation lives on the documentation site — this README is a doorway, not a duplicate.**
> ### 📖 https://fractalsynapse.github.io/dsh-chapters/
## Install (the whole setup)
[代码示例省略，未执行]

After restart you have the fork button, seven agent tools, twelve `/chapters-*` commands (through
`0

.2.17`, including `/chapters-remove`) — and the optional `chapters` preset that routes `/compact`
th
rough the zero-token engine.

## Developing / contributing
Three ways to set up a development environment — pick whichever fits your workflow:
| Mode | Best for | Command |
| **Centralized** (your live profile) | Day-to-day development on your main machine | `./dev/install

/install.sh && dsh web` |
| **Compartmentalized** (isolated DSH_HOME) | Testing changes without touc

hing your live sessions | `DSH_HOME=/tmp/dsh-dev ./dev/install/install.sh` |
| **Containerized** (fu
ll stack) | Isolated platform with vLLM + Playwright + Chromium | `cd dev/install && docker compose
) | Isolated platform with vLLM + Playwright + Chromium | `cd dev/install && docker compose up -d` |

All three install the same plugin set: dsh-chapters, dsh-codegraph
(structural code search via pre-i

ndexed AST graph), and dsh-tinyfish-search. Full details in
`dev/install/README.md`. The containeriz

ed stack additionally ships its own
vLLM model server (Qwen3-4B-AWQ with inference + systemone endpo

ints), a DSH Web UI service, and a
CI-capable test runner — everything runs locally with no external

service, and a
CI-capable test runner — everything runs locally with no external API keys required.
